case_studies.title: Cache-Aware Prompt Compression:A Two-Tier Cost Model for LLM API Caching
case_studies.abstract: Production LLM deployments combine two cost-reduction primitives: prompt caching (a discounted rate for re-used token prefixes) and prompt compression (fewer tokens sent). The compression literature has standardized on query-aware methods that produce a different compressed prefix per query, mechanically invalidating the prefix-strict cache on every call. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient caching in large language models by building a two-tier cost model for LLM API caching, which results in a better understanding of how caching works in these systems. The researchers found that the cache has a sharp threshold near 3,500 tokens, affecting its effectiveness. This research is relevant to IT engineers managing cloud infrastructure that uses LLM APIs.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM API deployments, here is what to do: review your caching strategy to account for the two-tier architecture, check your token usage to optimize caching effectiveness, and consider compressing prompts to reduce token count below the 3,500 token threshold.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: IT engineers may not know the caching characteristics of LLM APIs like Sonnet. Relevance: Focus on LLM API caching directly affects IT engineers' work. Value: Provides actionable insights on caching thresholds for LLM API deployments, which could inform IT decision-making.
